derivation: Anchors: 15 at 2022.15 [E-9516]; 67 at 2024.30 and >75 at 2024.95 (Agent B E-2071/E-2072 lineage); 117 at 2025.95 (Agent B E-2054). claim: Derived: at the observed doubling time and a 5 percent per year growth in the IND base, the AI-derived share of new clinical entries crosses 10 percent between about 2029 and 2033 and 50 percent between about 2032 and 2039, so the low-share ceiling on system-level effect is a statement about the present decade and not about 2035 or 2040.

derivation: Let g_AI = 2^(1/DT)-1 and g_base = 0.05. Relative share growth r = (1+g_AI)/(1+g_base)-1. DT=1.5 -> g_AI=0.587, r=0.511, share doubling 1.66 yr. DT=2.05 -> g_AI=0.409, r=0.342, share doubling 2.35 yr. Starting share 1.0 percent (global IND denominator) or 3.7 percent (US commercial IND denominator, 42 new entries in 2025 / 1139). Time to 10 percent: from 1.0 pct, 3.32 doublings = 5.5 yr (DT 1.5) to 7.8 yr (DT 2.05); from 3.7 pct, 1.43 doublings = 2.4 to 3.4 yr. Time to 50 percent: from 1.0 pct, 5.64 doublings = 9.4 to 13.3 yr; from 3.7 pct, 3.76 doublings = 6.2 to 8.8 yr. Union of brackets: 10 percent in 2029-2033, 50 percent in 2032-2039.

claim: Derived: about 85 percent of the druggable genome has never yielded an approved drug, and this population of never-prosecuted targets is invisible to per-programme cost, duration and attrition statistics, which are conditioned on a programme having started.

figures.sample: human druggable genome per NIH IDG classification

derivation: 700/4500 = 0.1556 targeted; 1-0.1556 = 0.844. Santos gives 667 human protein targets of approved drugs [E-9500], IDG gives fewer than 700 against about 4500 druggable-genome genes [E-9501]. The two agree to within 5 percent. This ratio is not itself an attrition statistic: no programme-level dataset records targets that were never prosecuted, so this bound is the only available proxy for the suppressed-programme channel.

claim: Derived: the AI cohort Phase II figure of about 40 percent is compared in the literature against a historical benchmark of about 37 percent, but the contemporaneous Citeline Phase II transition rate is 28 percent, so the comparator choice moves the sign of the apparent AI effect.
source_title: Comparator sensitivity of the AI Phase II success claim

figures.denominator_def: AI cohort Phase II success (0.40) minus contemporaneous Citeline Phase II transition (0.28)
figures.sample: AI cohort n approximately 8 completed Phase 2 assets; Citeline programme-level denominator

derivation: Against the historical 37 percent benchmark the AI-minus-benchmark difference is +0.03; against the contemporaneous 28 percent Citeline figure it is +0.12, a fourfold difference in effect size arising purely from comparator selection. Neither comparison is denominator-matched: the Citeline figure is a programme-level Phase II to Phase III transition and the AI figure's denominator is undisclosed. The correct conclusion is that no denominator-matched comparison exists in either direction, not that the effect is zero.
